column3: The Hebrew preserves the image “according to the mouth of the LORD.”
The Hebrew command “give us” is plural.
The Hebrew shifts from “us” to “me and my children and my livestock,” and says “brought us up.”
The Hebrew says “the river,” without explicitly naming the Nile.
The Hebrew says “on the rock,” rather than “by the rock.”
The Hebrew uses the collective names “Amalek” and “Israel.”
The Hebrew says “choose men for us,” rather than specifying “some of our men.”
The Hebrew has “his hand,” singular, in both clauses.
The Hebrew says “his people,” rather than “his army,” and retains the image of the sword’s mouth.
The Hebrew says “put it in Joshua’s ears,” rather than simply “recite it to Joshua.”
The Hebrew says “a hand on the throne,” without explicitly stating that it was lifted toward it.
